title: Coprime by Chance
statement: Two positive integers are chosen independently and uniformly from $\{1,\dots,N\}$. As $N\to\infty$, what does the probability that they are coprime approach? (Give a decimal.)
insight: Coprime means no prime divides both; divisibility by different primes is asymptotically independent, so multiply (1 − 1/p²) over primes.
redHerring: Counting pairs with gcd 1 directly with inclusion–exclusion over all integers, without seeing the product.
hints: What is the probability that a fixed prime $p$ divides both numbers?
Coprime means this fails for every prime. Treat the primes as independent.
solution:
A prime $p$ divides both numbers with probability $\tfrac1{p^2}$, and these events are asymptotically independent across primes. So

$P(\text{coprime}) = \prod_p\left(1 - \tfrac1{p^2}\right) = \tfrac1{\zeta(2)} = \tfrac6{\pi^2} \approx 0.6079$,

using the Euler product $\zeta(s) = \prod_p (1-p^{-s})^{-1}$.
